candidateAudit.text: Yesterday, Vienna City Hall became the setting for the 18th Diversity Ball—and what a beautiful celebration it was. People with different backgrounds, identities, experiences and ways of moving, communicating and experiencing music came together to celebrate. I especially appreciated that people with disabilities were present not only among the guests, but also as artists, performers and active participants throughout the evening. Inclusion felt like part of the event’s foundation—not an afterthought. That commitment could be felt in the many accessibility measures: Austrian Sign Language interpretation, accessible facilities, trained assistance, vibration vests through which music could be experienced physically, a Silent Disco and the Dunkelbar hosted by the Austrian Association Supporting the Blind and Visually Impaired. This is what meaningful inclusion looks like: creating a space in which people are considered from the beginning and can participate in ways that work for them. The evening was colourful, joyful and full of energy, but it also carried an important message. Diversity itself is not a barrier.
